title: A global section vanishing at every point of a quasi-compact scheme is nilpotent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is quasi-compact, and let $h\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\mathcal O_X(X)$. For $x\in X$ write $h(x)\in\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ [def-weil-residue-field] for the image of the germ $h_x\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$ in the residue field. If $h(x)=0$ for every $x\in X$ (equivalently $h_x\in\mathfrak m_x$, i.e. $h_x$ is not a unit of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, for every $x$), then $h$ is nilpotent: $h^n=0$ in $\mathcal O_X(X)$ for some $n\ge1$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.4 (Tag 03GY, lemma-stein-universally-closed), proof, surjectivity paragraph: 'h|_X is a global section of the structure sheaf of X which vanishes at every point. As X is quasi-compact this means that h|_X is a nilpotent section'

split_report.summary: The statement was wrong as written: 'the germ of h is zero in every stalk' means h = 0 by the sheaf property, which is not what Stacks 03GY uses. Corrected (content changed) to the intended statement of the source: h vanishes at every point, i.e. its image h(x) in the residue field kappa(x) is zero (h_x in m_x) for every x, on a quasi-compact X; then h is nilpotent. Added def-weil-residue-field to stmt_deps; source place made precise. Mathlib states exactly this (CompactSpace X; basicOpen f = ⊥ iff f(x) = 0 in every residue field; IsNilpotent f iff basicOpen f = ⊥), so the node is a Mathlib leaf (status mathlib, no proof steps); declarations read in the Mathlib source. The citer lem-weil-pbc-stein-universally-closed-factor step 4 says 'whose germ vanishes at every point' and should read 'whose image in every residue field kappa(x) vanishes' (reported, not edited).
